name.text: Image of a triangle under a matrix

questiontext.text:
The matrix \(M = {@Mt@}\) maps triangle ABC, with \(A({@A[1]@},\,{@A[2]@})\), \(B({@B[1]@},\,{@B[2]@})\) and \(C({@C[1]@},\,{@C[2]@})\), onto triangle \(A'B'C'\).

Find \(A'\), \(B'\) and \(C'\). Write them as the columns of a \(2 \times 3\) matrix, in the order \(A'\), \(B'\), \(C'\).

[[input:ans1]] [[validation:ans1]] [[feedback:prt1]]

generalfeedback.text:
Write the vertices as the columns of the object matrix and multiply by \(M\). Each column of the answer is the image of the vertex in that column.

\({@Mt@}{@Ob@} = {@ta@}\)

For A: \({@Mt@}{@cA@} = {@Mt.cA@}\), since the top row gives \(x' = {@xr@}\) and the bottom row gives \(y' = {@yr@}\). So \(A'\) is \(({@ta[1,1]@},\,{@ta[2,1]@})\), \(B'\) is \(({@ta[1,2]@},\,{@ta[2,2]@})\) and \(C'\) is \(({@ta[1,3]@},\,{@ta[2,3]@})\).

Sketch both triangles on squared paper to check: the origin O does not move under any matrix.

node.description: Columns of M used as rows

truefeedback.text: You used the columns of \(M\) as its rows, working out \(x' = {@xT@}\). Multiply each row of \(M\) by the column of the point: the top row gives \(x' = {@xr@}\).
You used only the numbers on the leading diagonal of \(M\). Every entry counts: \(x' = {@xr@}\) and \(y' = {@yr@}\).

falsefeedback.text: Write the vertices as the columns of a matrix and multiply by \(M\), row by column: for each vertex, \(x' = {@xr@}\) and \(y' = {@yr@}\).
